note: Sanderson argues that proofs generated without understanding no longer serve as a proxy for it, and proposes defining ‘motivated explanations’, which answer how one would come to think of an idea, and giving them academic credit comparable to solving open problems, noting that every AI-generated proof arrives as an unsolved exposition problem. He suggests practical steps such as PhD students presenting solutions as talks, written standards, journals devoted to understanding and more weight for exposition in hiring, and argues that visible cultural change could reassure prospective mathematicians.
title: If math is more than proof, we need to better celebrate the rest of it
who: Grant Sanderson (3Blue1Brown), guest post on Terence Tao’s blog
